info.title: Helix server integration API
info.description: Private-LAN server management API. Session cookie AND CSRF proof are required together; mutations and file commands require exact Origin. Account capabilities are not per-server credentials. All server routes are listed; broker response objects are not yet all fully typed. Consult per-server capabilities before acting. Do not automatically replay mutations or treat a job ID as completion.

post.summary: Run a permitted operation on a token-scoped server
post.description: Bearer token only. Cookie and Origin headers are rejected. See SERVER-TOKENS.md for operation fields and permissions. No host/global operations are allowed; job_status is restricted to this token's accepted jobs. Transfers (server_transfer_preflight, transfer_server_content) involve two servers: the token must list both, with files.read and view (preflight) or files.write (transfer); Full access covers all.

post.description: Do not replay on timeout, connection loss, or 5xx. Keep the returned job ID and poll it. An accepted job is not a completed operation. Kill is forceful; prefer stop. Update compatibility depends on the selected server software.

get.description: Poll with a bounded deadline and delay. HTTP 200 only means the job status was read, not that the job succeeded. Reaching a client deadline does not cancel the job. Retention is finite; an unknown job is not permission to repeat a mutation.

ServerToken.description: Server-scoped token; accepted only by /automation endpoints.

Origin.name: Origin
Origin.description: Exact configured Helix origin: scheme, host and port, without a trailing slash. Never spoof a different service's origin.

InstanceId.name: instance_id
InstanceId.description: Exact id returned by server inventory, including its manager prefix. Native IDs are helix:UUID. Never substitute a display name, bare registry UUID or filesystem path.

Problem.description: Error; branch on HTTP status and code, not message text. A mutation's outcome may be unknown after a timeout or transport error.

Retry-After.description: Present on selected capacity/rate errors. Does not make a mutation safe to replay.

BrokerObject.description: Broker result. The exact resource-specific fields remain documented in docs/API.md and tested in frontend adapters; this schema deliberately does not claim full generated-client coverage.

timezone.description: Must exactly match the host timezone returned by Helix.

schedule.description: State is none, unavailable, scheduled, or degraded. Scheduled states include the verified timezone, retention, unit state, and next activation.

password.description: At least five characters; creation may omit it for an automatically generated password.

modifiers.description: combat, deathpenalty, resources, raids and portals; publisher-supported values only.

ServerNetworkExposure.description: Public requests host firewall preparation only, never router forwarding.

TransferPart.description: plugins = plugin JARs and config files without databases or player data; plugin_data = everything under plugins/; mods = mods/*.jar; configs = bukkit/spigot/paper/purpur files and config/; server_properties = gameplay settings (the target keeps its ports, RCON, level name, seed, player limit, MOTD and whitelist); datapacks = the world's datapacks; player_lists = whitelist, ops and bans; worlds = replaces the target's worlds

target_id.description: Helix-managed target server, for example helix:UUID

remove_missing_jars.description: Also delete target plugin or mod JARs that the source does not have

ServerFileRequest.description: Relative paths only; empty path lists the server root. File access requires games.manage since files can contain secrets. Mutations to server files, upload_file and upload_finish require a stopped native server; upload staging can run while online. upload_file is content-idempotent up to 3 MiB; larger uploads resume matching staging by path, size, checksum and revision. Uploads use anonymous staging and checksum verification. See SERVER-API.md for recovery, limits and conflict handling.
